title: Private Endpoints and Private Link
description: Discover how Private Endpoints expose Azure services privately inside your VNet using Private Link.

data.text: Azure Private Link lets you access Azure PaaS services — like Storage, SQL, and Key Vault — over a private endpoint inside your VNet. The service gets a private IP address from your VNet, and traffic never traverses the public internet.
A private endpoint is a network interface that maps to an Azure service. It uses Azure Private Link to provide secure, private connectivity.

data.title: Benefits of Private Endpoints
items: Traffic stays on the Microsoft backbone network
No public IP exposure for the service
Works with on-premises via ExpressRoute or VPN

data.title: Create a Private Endpoint for Key Vault
data.content: Expose Key Vault privately inside your VNet.
data.code: az network private-endpoint create   --name myKvEndpoint   --resource-group myRG   --vnet-name myVNet   --subnet web-subnet   --private-connection-resource-id $(az keyvault show -n myKeyVault -g myRG --query id -o tsv)   --group-id vault   --connection-name myKvConnection

data.title: Private DNS
data.text: When you create a private endpoint, Azure can create a Private DNS zone that maps the service's public DNS name to the private IP. This lets your app use the same endpoint URL whether it is inside or outside the VNet.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Private endpoints give Azure services a private IP inside your VNet.
Private Link ensures traffic never uses the public endpoint.
Combine with Private DNS zones for seamless application configuration.
data.takeaway: Use private endpoints for any sensitive service: Key Vault, SQL, Storage, and APIs.
